newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-EALES'S INJURY SHAKES UNBEATEN WALLABIES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-EALES'S INJURY SHAKES UNBEATEN WALLABIES.

text.p: Tim Horan will take over the reins as Wallaby captain this week determined to preserve his side's unbeaten tour record in the absence of injured skipper John Eales.
Eales suffered a fractured eye socket in the 22-12 victory over Ireland at Lansdowne Road on Saturday, robbing Australia of their main line-out presence against Wales in Cardiff next Sunday.

After test wins in Italy, Scotland and Ireland, the Wallabies must also negotiate fixtures against Munster and the Barbarians if they want to complete a clean sweep and Horan acknowledges that the loss of Eales is significant.
"It's a huge blow," admitted Horan, after news of his fellow Queenslander's injury filtered through to his team mates as they prepared for the post-match banquet in Dublin.
"They originally thought he had a bruised cornea and that he would be fit for the Welsh game. Now they say it'll be around six to eight weeks before it heals."

Hailed as the outstanding forward in the world, Eales will undergo further medical tests in Ireland and is likely to stay with the tour party. His injury occurred midway through the second-half when he was tackled high by Irish centre Mark McCall but there have been no Wallaby suggestions of malice.
Five Australian players have now been ruled out of the trip and, at the end of a hectic year, the strain of professional rugby is beginning to show.

Before they flew to Europe they had already met Wales and Canada and competed in the Tri-Nation series with New Zealand and South Africa inside three months. Horan, though, insists there is still something left in the tank.
"The guys are pretty tired but when we have to dig deep the fitness is there," he said. "Winning all the tests here is very important to us."

Uncapped lock David Giffin is likely to partner Warwick Waugh in the second-row against Wales, who will have to perform well to match the fervour of the Irish pack on a bitterly cold Dublin afternoon.
Full-back Jim Staples is likely to be out for at least three months after breaking a bone in his wrist but hooker and new captain Keith Wood believes Ireland's future is at last looking brighter.
"We are getting there but it's a professional game and we didn't finish the job," said Wood, an odds-on certainty for a place on the Lions tour to South Africa next year.
"It's so difficult to beat a side like Australia. Their defence is superb."
